name: Going
subcategory: trip planning, navigation and travel intelligence
tagline: Save user-found fare ideas and maintain a destination watchlist without claiming live deals

tiers.name: Limited
tiers.limits: Domestic economy deal alerts from airports in the contiguous US; 0 international, mistake-fare, points, or premium-cabin alerts

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: Domestic and international economy deals, points-and-miles economy deals, mistake fares in all cabins, and custom mobile alerts

tiers.name: Elite
tiers.limits: Everything in Premium plus business-, first-, and premium-economy deal alerts

pricing.freeTierCaps: Limited plan: domestic economy alerts from the contiguous US only; 0 international, mistake-fare, points-and-miles, premium-economy, business, or first-class alerts.
pricing.billingTerms: annual only; no monthly plan; paid plans auto-renew after a 14-day trial
pricing.hiddenCosts: Cancellation/refund handling differs by purchase channel: mobile stores can require full-refund handling while direct web subscriptions may use prorated treatment.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Going, save user-found fare ideas and maintain a destination watchlist without claiming live deals. The hard boundary is fare-monitoring operation, editorial curation, member scale, and airline pricing data, plus proprietary live data and network coverage.
coreLoopDIY: Save user-found fare ideas, maintain a destination watchlist, map user-entered places and reservations, and keep an offline itinerary without claiming live deals or proprietary availability.
requirements: optional public transit or weather API
whatYouLose: fare-monitoring operation, editorial curation, member scale, and airline pricing data
booking, disruption support, and offline map fleet
moatNotes: proprietary live data and network coverage
ongoingBurden: map licensing, fare feeds, reservation access, route freshness, disruptions, geocoding, caching, offline data, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Going because travel subscriptions sell current data and confidence during disruption, not just an itinerary list. The recurring cost buys map licensing, fare feeds, reservation access, route freshness, disruptions, geocoding, caching, offline data, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Wanderer
priorArt.desc: Open-source self-hosted trail database and route explorer using open map data.

alternatives.name: Google Flights
alternatives.desc: Free route and fare tracking; Google already owns the servers and probably the rest of the itinerary.

facts.install: Open Google Flights in a browser; sign in to create tracked routes or specific-flight price alerts
facts.dataFormat: Tracked routes, dates, flights, and notification settings live in the user's Google account; alerts arrive by email rather than as user-owned files.
facts.gapVsPaid: Google Flights gives excellent route and fare tracking, but it does not replace Going's human-curated stream of unusually good fares and mistake-deal judgement.
facts.setupBlocker: A Google account is required for durable alerts, and the user must define routes or dates instead of receiving a human-curated deal feed.

alternatives.name: KAYAK
alternatives.desc: Free route alerts and saved trips, funded by the booking links it keeps showing you.

alternatives.name: Skyscanner
alternatives.desc: A free fare wishlist with alerts; the recommendations are affiliate-shaped, not charitable.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium plan and a personal itinerary organizer DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Going in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, MapLibre GL, and user-supplied map and travel APIs; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: save user-found fare ideas, maintain a destination watchlist, map user-entered places and reservations, and keep an offline itinerary without claiming live deals or proprietary availability.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create trips, days, places, reservations, notes, documents, packing items, and emergency contacts.
Geocode only user-entered places and display them through MapLibre with cached trip-area tiles where allowed.
Parse forwarded reservation text locally into editable fields without logging message content.
Build a day timeline, route overview, conflict warnings, timezone display, and offline printable itinerary.
Allow manual updates for delays and reservations and label all external data with source and timestamp.
Export a complete trip bundle as JSON, calendar file, Markdown, and PDF.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out live flight, hotel, award, or ticket inventory.
Deliberately leave out commercial turn-by-turn navigation and global offline maps.
Deliberately leave out booking guarantees, disruption rebooking, and traveler support.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
